description: CatBoost agent-tune (agent_file_protocol scout+combine+iters) of the 3 H=200 cells vs the CatBoost sweep and the XGBoost agent. V1.5_TBD #1 — fills the last cell of the _268 2x2. All current vintage, date-aligned, test window 2023-07-27..2024-10-03.
metric: R-Precision@K (per-day fixed K, macro over days R_q>0, min(K,R_q) denominator)
finding: Tuning the robust backend (CatBoost) at H=200 is HIGH-VARIANCE: 1/3 cells (sp500/50) decisively beat the cheap sweep (@1 0.930 vs 0.630), 2/3 (russell, sp500/40) LOST @1 to the sweep's plain defaults. All 3 had near-identical eval@1 (0.805-0.845) and near-identical HP, but test@1 ranged 0.557->0.930 — the outcome is set entirely by eval->test decay direction (sp500/50 strengthened into the bull test window, decay -0.085; the others over-fit, decay +0.24), which the agent cannot see. Same eval->test-decay disease as _268's XGBoost, milder. CatBoost-agent beat XGBoost-agent @1 on 2/3 but still lost to the CatBoost SWEEP on 2/3.
verdict: The CatBoost <=3-iter sweep remains the robust H=200 default. Agent-tuning CatBoost is opportunistic (real upside on sp500/50) but NOT a reliable improvement; always validate the agent pick vs the sweep on test. The root cause is the eval-R-p@1 objective being an unreliable single-window proxy at long horizons (afflicts both backends) — fix = multi-window/decay-penalized eval (V1.5_TBD #2).
followup: V1.5_TBD #2 (multi-window eval objective) is the real fix; promote before further H=200 agent-tuning.
